exposure: Obstetric violence (physical or psychological violence, disrespect, lack of information, lack of privacy and communication with the healthcare team, inability to ask questions, and loss of autonomy)
cohort: 20,527 puerperal women and their newborns from the "Birth in Brazil" study.
finding: Obstetric violence during childbirth was associated with a decreased probability of exclusive breastfeeding at hospital discharge, particularly for women who had a vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Obstetric violence had a stronger negative effect on breastfeeding at discharge for women who had a vaginal birth compared to those who had a cesarean birth.
